stacks.name: User-interface sans
stacks.note: Starting with system-ui hands iOS and macOS their San Francisco face, which has no public name. The named fonts are what each platform offers next.

stacks.name: Condensed sans
stacks.note: Nothing on Android is condensed. Roboto is the fallback so text still fits the same family.

stacks.name: Didone serif
stacks.note: Only Apple ships a true didone. Constantia and Georgia keep the contrast high elsewhere.

stacks.name: Slab serif
stacks.note: Only Apple platforms carry a slab; the rest fall to a plain serif.

stacks.name: Rounded sans
stacks.note: Rounded faces exist only on Apple platforms.

fonts.name: Apple Braille
fonts.note: Dot patterns for the embossed Braille cell.

fonts.name: Bodoni 72
fonts.note: Apple lists this as a macOS system font only, although it ships on iOS too.

fonts.name: Ebrima
fonts.note: Also covers N'Ko, Tifinagh, Vai and Osmanya.

fonts.name: Helvetica Neue
fonts.note: The iOS UI face is San Francisco, reached with system-ui rather than by name.

fonts.name: Leelawadee UI
fonts.note: Also covers Lao, Khmer and Buginese.

fonts.name: Noto Sans CJK
fonts.note: Also installed under the names Noto Sans CJK JP, KR, SC and TC.

fonts.name: Noto Serif CJK
fonts.note: Also installed under the names Noto Serif CJK JP, KR, SC and TC.

fonts.name: Roboto Flex
fonts.note: Variable; the Android 14 and later UI face.

fonts.name: Segoe UI
fonts.note: The Windows UI face; system-ui resolves to it on Windows 10.

fonts.name: Segoe UI Historic
fonts.note: Historic scripts such as Runic, Ogham and Old Italic.

fonts.name: Segoe UI Variable
fonts.note: Windows 11 uses this as its UI face. The Display, Text and Small axes are optical sizes.
